methods.label: Rewrite negative powers as reciprocals
methods.explanation:
A negative first power means a reciprocal. The original expression therefore requires \(x\ne0\), \(y\ne0\), and \(x+y\ne0\). Combining the two reciprocals reveals a factor that can cancel:
\[
x^{-1}+y^{-1}
=\frac1x+\frac1y
=\frac{x+y}{xy}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
(x+y)^{-1}(x^{-1}+y^{-1})
=\frac1{x+y}\cdot\frac{x+y}{xy}
=\frac1{xy}
=x^{-1}y^{-1}.
\]
The cancellation is valid because \(x+y\ne0\). With all three original restrictions retained, the simplified expression is \(x^{-1}y^{-1}\), choice C.
